name: Bitstream Overloading via Flush Bytes and Markers
definition: A technique to partition a single arithmetic-coded bitstream into semantically disjoint, independently accessible segments. It solves the problem that arithmetic coders buffer bits into byte-sized units, making individual symbols or small groups of symbols inaccessible without decoding the entire preceding stream.
summary: Bitstream Overloading partitions a single arithmetic-coded bitstream into independently accessible segments using flush bytes and markers, differing from sibling methods by operating at the entropy coding layer.
